key_insight: OnTrack streams agent trajectories in real time and flags likely failure by comparing each step against successful references, tool structure, or even raw logs, enabling millisecond-scale intervention before damage accumulates.
engineering_relevance: This gives operators a lightweight safety layer for autonomous LLM systems that can reduce wasted compute and block risky actions without paying the latency and cost of a second model on every step.
method: Monitors step-by-step trajectories against prior successful runs using streaming structure-aware optimal transport.
Supports three access regimes: full reference access, tool-schema-only access, and log-only monitoring.
Can alert, slow, or abort agents when it detects plan violations, loops, stalls, or repeated tool calls.
evidence_signal: On SWE-bench trajectories, using only the first 8 steps, OnTrack ranked failing runs below successful ones better than content-similarity baselines by +0.057 AUROC and saved about 18% of compute with 5 of 6 aborts correctly targeting failures.
watch_item: Performance and reliability depend on how much prior structure is available, so log-only settings may miss subtle failures and false aborts remain a practical deployment concern.
paper_title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport
